_comment: The mark type table — THE SHARED SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Java implementation
Why a separate file rather than an ordinary conformance vector: vectors contain operations
that have ALREADY BEEN CREATED, so they pin the anchor sides chosen at generation time. This
table is used when CREATING an operation — changing it on one side changes not a single
vector while changing how the editor behaves. The divergence would surface only in front of
a user, as "bold grows as I type on my side and not on yours".
The schema/ directory is outside the vector corpus deliberately: both sides load
conformance/*.json as vectors, and this is not a vector.
suggest-insert and suggest-delete (CP23) do not expand for the reason a link does not:
typing after a proposed insertion is ordinary writing, not part of somebody's proposal, and
a mark that swallowed it would put a stranger's text inside a suggestion they never made.
